newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says will increase Albania troops for vote.
newsitem.headline: Italy says will increase Albania troops for vote.

text.p: Italy said on Wednesday it would send more troops to a multinational force it is leading in Albania to boost security for planned June 29 elections.
Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini told reporters in the Sicilian capital Palermo that the extra soldiers would only remain in the Balkan country for a brief time.

"Together with Defence Minister (Beniamino) Andreatta, we are already planning a greater presence in the two weeks spanning the elections to guarantee safety in all areas where voting takes place," Dini said on the margin of a conference.
"After the elections, which we want to be free, fair and honest, the military presence will be ended swiftly," Dini said.

Italy has said it only wants the 6,500-strong force to stay in Albania for about a month after the vote, which is seen as an essential step towards normality after anarchy swept the country in March following the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.

Dini had no immediate details of how many more soldiers would be sent or whether other countries taking part in the force would send extra men. Italy has contributed some 2,500 soldiers to the security force, which began deploying in April.
Dini said it was "essential" for elections to go ahead on June 29.
Italy was due later on Wednesday to name a new ambassador to Tirana, following a diplomatic debacle.

The incumbent, Paolo Foresti, was due to have been replaced last week after an Albanian newspaper accused him of bias in favour of Albanian President Sali Berisha and of trying to undermine the role of European mediator Franz Vranitzky.
But his successor, Manfredo Inciso di Camerana, resigned 48 hours after his appointment after he was quoted by Italian daily La Repubblica as criticising Foresti and the foreign ministry.
